We present a 54-year-old caucasian man with a history of SPS and CVID. Other
pertinent medical history includes COPD with a 20-pack-year history of tobacco smoking,
occupational exposure to epoxy and fumes, and sleep apnea. He reported dyspnea when lying
down sleeping and at rest. The patient reported difficulty sleeping, walking around his block, and
lifting objects, including his newborn child, due to muscle stiffness. He had decreased
immunoglobulin levels in his blood and has had recurrent respiratory infections, sinusitis, and
pneumonia. On physical examination, he had coarse breath sounds, finger clubbing, and an oxygen
saturation of 90%. Pulmonary function testing, with spirometry and impulse oscillometry,
demonstrated a moderate obstructive ventilatory defect, airways hyperresponsiveness, and distal
airways narrowing. Our patient has been treated with high doses of IgG concurrently with rituximab
for the past 2 years, resulting in decreasing muscle stiffness. However, the patient recently reported
increased dyspnea and has continued using supplemental oxygen following a motor vehicle
accident, which required spinal surgery. We have initiated a subcutaneous IgG infusion 10%
(Human) with rHuPH20 to maintain consistent levels. This case highlights obstacles and unique
solutions necessitated by patients with multiple rare conditions.
